newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity steady with weather hold pattern.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity steady with weather hold pattern.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) held steady Thursday with little change in the state's weather, industry sources said.

The outage at Texas Utilities 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear unit 2 after a lightning strike Wednesday had little impact on prices, with the unit expected to return to service Thursday, the sources said.
Next-day on-peak ERCOT power was talked steady in the $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range for a 12-hour block, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next-day power was pegged in the $12.00-13.50 range, the sources said.
September on-peak electricity was said to be steady in the $20.25-20.50 range, while October was steady in the $17.75-18.10 range, the brokers and marketers said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
